## Grammar and design choices:

Gray supports numbers, strings, booleans, and null. Here is it’s expression grammar

expression → literal | unary | binary | grouping ;  
literal → NUMBER | STRING | "true" | "false" | "null" ;  
unary → ( "-" | "\!" ) expression ;  
binary → expression operator expression ;  
grouping → "(" expression ")" ;  
operator → "+" | "-" | "\*" | "/"  
         | "==" | "\!=" | "\<" | "\<=" | "\>" | "\>="  
         | "and" | "or" ;

Unary operators are negation and logical not (- and \!). Binary operators represent arithmetic, equality, comparisons, and logical operations. Compared to lox, gray uses null instead of nil and includes and and or. The grammar follows Lox so far and doesn’t care about precedence or associativity. The hard-coded ASTs determine their hierarchy and the nodes store expressions without evaluating them. 

## Dependency/setup instructions:

From the repo root run python test/lab2/test\_ast.py

## Tests:

1  
Purpose: Nested arithmetic, unary minus, and grouping

Binary(Unary(op(MINUS, "-"), Literal(123)), op(STAR, "\*"), Grouping(Literal(45.67)))

2  
Purpose: Addition, subtraction, and division

Binary(Binary(Literal(10), op(PLUS, "+"), Literal(2)), op(SLASH, "/"), Grouping(Binary(Literal(8), op(MINUS, "-"), Literal(4))))

3  
Purpose: Logical operators, negation, and booleans

Binary(Unary(op(BANG, "\!"), Literal(False)), op(AND, "and"), Grouping(Binary(Literal(True), op(OR, "or"), Literal(False))))

4  
Purpose: String equality

Binary(Literal("hello"), op(EQUAL\_EQUAL, "=="), Literal("hello"))

5  
Purpose: Null and inequality. Empty string

Binary(Literal(None), op(BANG\_EQUAL, "\!="), Literal(""))

6  
Purpose: Less than

Binary(Literal(1), op(LESS, "\<"), Literal(2))

7  
Purpose: Less than or equal

Binary(Literal(2), op(LESS\_EQUAL, "\<="), Literal(2))

8  
Purpose: Greater than

Binary(Literal(3), op(GREATER, "\>"), Literal(2))

9  
Purpose: Greater than or equal

Binary(Literal(3), op(GREATER\_EQUAL, "\>="), Literal(3))

10  
String escapes:

Literal('First\\n"second"\\\\third')

11  
Nested grouping and zero

Grouping(Grouping(Literal(0)))

## Limitations:

Parsing and execution still aren’t implemented. The grammar doesn’t specify precedence or associativity. All tests passed.
